name: dqlite
tagline: Canonical's embeddable C library that makes SQLite highly available with Raft replication.
description: dqlite (distributed SQLite) is a C library from Canonical that embeds a replicated SQL engine directly in your application: instances of the app form a Raft cluster and keep identical SQLite databases, with automatic leader election and failover and no external database to operate. It uses libuv and a custom wire protocol tuned for SQLite primitives, and Canonical ships it inside LXD and MicroK8s (where it replaces etcd as the Kubernetes datastore via kine). A Go binding (go-dqlite) is the main way to use it. It is a specialist building block for clustered infrastructure software rather than a standalone database server.

scale.notes: Small Raft clusters (3-5 voters) inside an application; each node holds the full database.

strengths: Embedded HA SQL with no separate database process
Raft-based automatic failover and leader election
Proven inside LXD and MicroK8s clusters
Small footprint suitable for edge appliances
weaknesses: Go is the only first-class high-level binding
Write throughput bounded by a single Raft leader
Small community outside Canonical's own products
useCases: Cluster state for infrastructure software (LXD, MicroK8s)
Kubernetes datastore replacement for etcd via kine
HA configuration stores in edge appliances
Embedding a replicated database in Go services
notIdealFor: Large datasets or high write rates
Teams wanting a standalone database server
